# Published, and referenced by nothing in this repo.
#
# Generated by measurement, not by hand: every asset under website/ whose
# basename appears in no .html/.css/.js/.ts/.tsx/.md/.py/.yml/... file in the
# tree. Pinned by site/test/payload_budget.test.js, which fails on a NEW
# entry and equally on a STALE one.
#
# Total: 20.5 MB across 22 files.
# The site itself loads in ~58 KB — none of this is on the critical path.
#
# THE DECISION, AND WHY IT IS NOT "DELETE THEM"
# ---------------------------------------------
# This file used to end "removing one is the operator's call". It was left open
# on the reasoning that a tweet or a deck could link one and be invisible from
# in here. That reasoning was never measured. It has been now, and the answer
# changes the question rather than settling it.
#
#   1. NOTHING HAS EVER REFERENCED THEM. All 427 commits were searched, every
#      text file in each, for all 22 basenames. Zero hits outside this list.
#      Not "unreferenced today" — never referenced, by any page this repo has
#      ever published. They arrived together in 6645bab, a 1,833-file bulk
#      import, and no page was ever written that would teach anyone the URL.
#      (The search was canary-checked against demo-recording, a live asset it
#      finds immediately — a scan that finds nothing proves nothing.)
#
#   2. DELETING THEM WOULD SAVE ZERO BYTES FOR ANYONE. The blobs are in git
#      history permanently; the pack is 77.6 MiB either way. The box deploys by
#      `git fetch <url> && git reset --hard`, so it downloads them regardless of
#      whether HEAD still lists them. The only thing deletion changes is 21 MB
#      of working tree — and the possibility of a 404 on a hand-shared URL.
#
# So the premise of the concern was wrong: this was never publish weight. It is
# history weight, and it is already spent. Deleting buys nothing measurable and
# risks something real, so they stay. The ratchet above keeps the pile from
# growing, which was always the part that mattered.
#
# If the operator disagrees, recovery is exact and one command per file:
#     git show 6645bab:website/qr_bot.png > website/qr_bot.png
#
# Several of these will also never be referenced BY DESIGN, and reading the
# list as 22 mistakes gets that wrong. The header images are sized for
# uploading to other platforms — mule_page_header_1600x600 and
# website_header_2400x800 are dimensions, not filenames — so the copy that
# matters lives on those platforms and this is the source. The infographics
# (13 MB of the 20.5) are deck material. A future "cleanup" should know that
# before treating the list as a to-do.
